cita: Zhao et al. (2026). Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering.
problema: Explicit textual procedural memory (RAG-style workflows/insights) causes a text-action disconnect: agents comprehend retrieved instructions but fail to consistently act on them, since procedural knowledge is inherently ineffable and lossy once compressed into discrete tokens.
mecanismo: Neural Procedural Memory (NPM) extracts dual-granularity contrastive experience (inter-trajectory: failed vs successful runs; intra-trajectory: degenerate vs effective steps within one failed run) into per-layer hidden-state representations; at inference it retrieves the top-K most similar historical tasks, synthesizes a task-specific steering vector from the retrieved contrastive pairs, and additively injects it into the residual stream at a target layer during generation, training-free and without consuming context-window tokens.
evaluacion: ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld and BabyAI with MiniCPM3-4B and Qwen3-4B/8B backbones, compared against No-Memory, explicit-text baselines (Insights, Workflows), other implicit-steering baselines (CAA, Mass-Mean), a Hybrid (NPM+Workflows) condition, plus PCA and cosine-similarity representational analyses of the extracted vectors.
numeros_clave: Qwen3-8B average score rises 30.63->36.32 with NPM vs CAA 22.79 / Mass-Mean 31.89; Hybrid (NPM+Workflows) reaches avg 41.89 (ALFWorld 66.42%, ScienceWorld 31.89); on WebShop/Qwen3-4B NPM scores 48.00, exceeding explicit Workflows' 45.73 (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper argues procedural knowledge represented as opaque activation-space steering vectors (not typed textual docs) outperforms text-based memory (§1, Table 1), challenging MF's Tier-1 'docs=truth, typed narrative' design for procedural facets specifically.
Implicit steering matches or beats explicit textual memory while consuming zero context-window tokens (§4.2), supporting MF's context-economy stance that not all memory needs to occupy the prompt.

Retrieval is a measured top-K historical-task similarity step that feeds vector synthesis (§3.3), an alternative measured-retrieval design operating over activations rather than text/embeddings of docs.

notes: Table 1 (4 benchmarks x 3 backbones) and Fig.4-5 (PCA/cosine-similarity structure of steering vectors) anchor the numbers; a genuinely different representation modality (activation space, not text or vector DB).

problema: Textual in-context skills are bottlenecked by the model's ability to comprehend and follow complex instructions in long contexts, and existing text-space skill-evolution methods remain decoupled from the underlying model's own learning.
mecanismo: A hypernetwork converts a textual skill (via a frozen text encoder) into LoRA-adapter parameters in a single forward pass, requiring no gradient updates and no context tokens at deployment; it is trained via skill-reconstruction pretraining (full/prefix/section-completion self-supervised objectives) then skill-exploitation fine-tuning on single/multi-turn trajectories, supports merging multiple parametric skills via rank-concatenation of LoRA factors, and includes a self-evolving loop (generate text skill -> verify -> revise -> recompile to parameters) with a continual variant that EMA-merges accepted task skills into one global parametric skill.
evaluacion: Six complex SWE subtasks judged by DeepSeek-V4-Flash (LLM judge), BERTScore and F1 against In-Context, SHINE and No-Skill baselines; a 529-task multi-skill-merging benchmark; self-evolution on HumanEval (up to 5 rounds) with an online continual-merging variant.
numeros_clave: ParametricSkills averages +6.44 LLM-judge points over In-Context (64.09 vs 57.65), beating No-Skill (50.21) and SHINE (48.48); rank-concat merge avg-judge 60.12 vs single-skill 58.27; self-evolution raises HumanEval pass rate from 75.00% (base parametric skill, 123/164) to 84.76% (139/164).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The skill still lives once as text and is recompiled into parameters only on demand (Fig.1), an alternative single-source-of-truth pattern where the compiled artifact is never itself the source of record, relevant to MF's multi-store-seams question.
The continual-learning variant EMA-merges accepted per-task parametric skills into one global skill (§3.4), a concrete consolidation mechanism operating in parameter space rather than text.

Self-evolving skills are still authored/revised as text and only compiled to parameters after verifier acceptance (§3.4), so provenance stays anchored in an inspectable textual artifact even though execution is parametric.

notes: Table 1 (six SWE subtasks) and Table 3 (HumanEval self-evolution) anchor the numbers; representacion=PARAMETROS is the differentiator vs typical text/vector memory stores.

cita: Zhou et al. (2026). ToM-SWE: User Mental Modeling for Software Engineering Agents.
problema: Coding agents operate statelessly session-to-session and lack mechanisms to infer and track evolving user intent, goals, preferences and constraints, especially under underspecified instructions, causing wasted effort and misaligned output.
mecanismo: A dedicated theory-of-mind (ToM) agent runs alongside the primary SWE agent, maintaining a three-tier external hierarchical memory (raw session storage; per-session user-model analysis; an aggregated overall cross-session user model). The SWE agent calls consult_tom in-session to receive user mental-state suggestions, and update_memory after each session to trigger the ToM agent's tiered update workflow (analyze_session then initialize/update the overall user model).
evaluacion: Ambiguous SWE-bench and a newly introduced Stateful SWE-bench (500 instances, 15 synthetic developer profiles, LLM user simulator) against CodeAct and RAGCodeAct baselines across 3 backbones, plus a 3-week/17-developer/209-session in-the-wild deployment study and a cost-overhead analysis.
numeros_clave: Stateful SWE-bench: ToMCodeAct 59.7% resolved vs CodeAct 18.1% (Claude Sonnet 4, +41.6pp); Ambiguous SWE-bench 63.4% vs 51.9%; user-satisfaction score 3.62 vs 2.57 (+41%); 86% of 174 ToM suggestions across 209 sessions accepted/partially accepted; ToM overhead ~16% of the SWE agent's average cost.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The three-tier hierarchical external memory (raw session / per-session model / overall model, Fig.2) separating raw evidence from a distilled narrative is directly analogous to MF's typed-doc-tiering design.

After-session consolidation aggregates per-session user models into the overall model only via an explicit LLM-driven update/initialize action (not passive accumulation), confirming MF's stance that promotion to durable memory should be a deliberate step.

The paper reports ToM overhead as roughly 16% of the SWE agent's average cost (§5.3) without a directional verdict on whether that overhead is acceptable, leaving it context rather than confirming or refuting a cost stance.

notes: Fig.4 and Table 1-2 (benchmark results) plus the cost Pareto-frontier figure (§5.3) anchor the numbers; the 3-week/17-developer field study (86% acceptance) is the qualitative evidence.

cita: Jayanti and Han (2026). Enhancing Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Context-Aware Server Collaboration.
problema: Traditional MCP keeps servers stateless and forces every coordination step through a central LLM that must hold the full context/state in its window, causing high latency, repeated inference calls, and context loss between steps in multi-agent workflows.
mecanismo: CA-MCP introduces a Shared Context Store (SCS) that the central LLM seeds once with an initial plan (goals, constraints, execution outline); MCP servers then become autonomous stateful reactors that read/write the SCS directly to coordinate intermediate state and outputs, without repeated round-trips to the central LLM, which only re-engages at the end to summarize the accumulated context into a final response.
evaluacion: TravelPlanner (500 queries: execution time, completeness, BERTScore, ROUGE-L, LLM-call count) and REALM-Bench Wedding Logistics P5 (goal/constraint satisfaction, makespan, coordination score, LLM calls), comparing Traditional MCP vs CA-MCP with paired significance tests.
numeros_clave: TravelPlanner: execution time 41.99s->13.52s (67.8% faster, paired t-test p=1.6e-137); completeness 0.764->1.000; LLM calls 5->2 (60% reduction); REALM-Bench: makespan 330->180 min (45.5% shorter), execution time 8.52s->2.26s (73.5% faster), LLM calls halved 2->1.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Shared Context Store persists intermediate task/plan state (goals, constraints, execution outline) written once by the planner LLM and read/updated by servers throughout execution (§2), a direct instance of plan-state as first-class shared memory across agents.

Replacing per-server private context with one shared blackboard-style store (single source of truth for task state) empirically halves LLM calls while improving completeness (Table 2-3), supporting MF's single-source-per-fact stance over duplicated per-agent stores.

Measured wall-clock/latency and LLM-call reductions (67.8%/73.5% faster, Fig.2-3) evidence that centralizing shared state, instead of re-sending full context each step, is a concrete context-economy lever.

notes: Table 2 (TravelPlanner) and Table 3 (REALM-Bench) anchor the numbers; small-scale paper (anonymous GitHub repo, only 2 benchmark tasks, authors explicitly note no hardware/parallelism controls in Limitations) -- RECONSIDERAR generalizability.

cita: Anderson (2026). The AI Codebase Maturity Model: From Assisted Coding to Fully Autonomous Systems.
problema: Teams adopting AI coding tools plateau at ad-hoc 'prompt and review' without a systematic framework for progressing toward more autonomous, trustworthy AI-driven development, and existing maturity models define levels by autonomy alone rather than by the feedback infrastructure that makes autonomy safe.
mecanismo: A 6-level maturity model (Assisted -> Instructed -> Measured -> Adaptive -> Semi-Automated -> Fully Autonomous) defined by feedback-loop topology: each level encodes human judgment into durable artifacts (instruction files -> metrics/tests -> self-tuning configs -> proposal pipelines -> a multi-agent fleet with a distributed work ledger 'Beads' for claiming work plus a workload governor that adapts cadence to backlog), validated by a 4-month practitioner case study and a reference multi-agent implementation (Hive).
evaluacion: 4-month longitudinal practitioner case study on KubeStellar Console (36+ cataloged feedback loops mapped to ACMM levels) plus initial production-deployment evidence for the Hive Level-6 reference implementation, including specific bug-fix case studies.
numeros_clave: 91% code coverage across 12 shards; 74 CI/CD workflows, 32 nightly test suites, 36+ cataloged feedback loops; bug-to-fix under 30 minutes and feature-to-implementation under 60 minutes, 24/7; Case A external bug fixed/merged in 3 hours (624 additions across 7 files); Case B user-misunderstanding response in 10 minutes.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Level 6's Beads distributed work ledger lets agents claim/track work-in-progress state to prevent duplicate effort, and an adaptive workload governor tracks backlog state (SURGE/BUSY/QUIET/IDLE) to set cadence, both concrete instances of plan/task state as first-class shared memory.

The model's central thesis, that each level's capability must be encoded into a durable artifact (instructions -> tests -> configs -> policy files) rather than held only in a human's head or the model's context, directly supports MF's promotion-of-gotchas-to-recipes stance.

The paper's headline lesson (Level 3 section) is that flaky/non-deterministic tests erode the trust required for autonomous merges, reinforcing MF's concern that memory/automation artifacts need reliability guarantees, not just presence.

notes: Table 1-2 (level/feedback-loop inventory) and the Case A/B examples anchor the numbers; single-practitioner, self-authored experience report (IBM Research, written with Claude Code assistance per its own disclosure), not peer-reviewed -- RECONSIDERAR given the n=1, self-reported nature of the evidence.

cita: Jiang et al. (2026). KRCA: An Efficient Root Cause Analysis System in Hyper-Scale Microservice Systems via Agentic AI.
problema: Root-cause analysis in hyper-scale (200,000+ service) microservice systems is bottlenecked by extreme dynamism (no time budget for model retraining) and massive scale (400+ metrics per service), pushing LLMs into a 'lost in the middle' hallucination failure mode when reasoning directly over raw anomalous-metric sets.
mecanismo: A 3-stage pipeline: (1) API-level drilldown recursively scores/prunes downstream APIs by failure-rate/latency correlation to isolate suspicious services; (2) anomalous metrics are mapped onto a generic 4-type causal skeleton (External/Internal/Dependency/KPI) to instantiate a high-recall initial causal graph without expensive statistical causal discovery; (3) a multi-agent framework (Main Agent plus domain Sub Agents) refines the graph via a three-tiered memory (Working, Factual, Experiential) that retrieves similar historical failure cases and reasoning insights through a weighted composite RAG scheme to support evidence-based verification and self-reflection.
evaluacion: 300 real-world production failures at Kuaishou, measured by AC@1/AC@3 accuracy for root-cause service localization and failure-type classification against baselines (incl. RCA-Agent), an ablation removing drilldown / skeleton-graph / multi-agent / tiered-memory / using naive RAG, and 6+ months of live production deployment.
numeros_clave: KRCA AC@1 0.88 (service localization) / 0.79 (failure-type classification), beating strongest baseline RCA-Agent by >=31/32 absolute points; production deployment reduces average diagnosis time by 77.3% over 6+ months, processing 2,000+ alerts/day; ablation shows disabling Tiered Memory or replacing it with Naive RAG both cause consistent AC@1/AC@3 drops (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: An ablation explicitly measures that a naive flat-similarity RAG underperforms the structured tiered-retrieval scheme (Table 2, w/ Naive RAG row), direct evidence that retrieval DESIGN, not just presence, is measurably load-bearing, reinforcing ADR-019.

The three-tiered memory (Working/Factual/Experiential) separating live working state from durable factual/experiential knowledge, refreshed via self-reflection after each case, is a production-proven tiering pattern MF could examine.
Production deployment reports a 77.3% reduction in diagnosis time over 6+ months at 2,000+ alerts/day, hard evidence that a well-designed retrieval-augmented memory reduces operational cost at scale.

notes: Table 1 (main AC@1/AC@3 results) and Table 2 (ablation, w/o Tiered Memory / w/ Naive RAG rows) anchor the numbers; Fig.6 describes the three-tiered Working/Factual/Experiential memory architecture.
